reuse.why: Server call sites are routed through getScheduledAmount, but the API's expectedAmount writes its own amount resolution instead of calling it, and the approximate tolerance is re-coded as Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) instead of the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts.

duplication.why: Two rule copies are added: the null/number/range dispatch in scheduleModel.toExternal and the 7.5% tolerance inside getScheduledAmount, both already defined elsewhere in the tree.

placement.why: The rule correctly lands in shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount, but the API model in server/api-models.ts carries its own copy of the rule instead of delegating to that shared definition.

scope.why: Changes are about the expected-amount rule, the API field and their type adjustments; the API test asserts a stale step-2 rule but is in scope.

maintainability.why: After step 4 the API's expectedAmount still applies the furthest-from-zero rule while every other path uses the lowest-allowed rule, showing the copy already drifted; the tolerance constant now lives in two places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount with its own nested ternary instead of getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount, false, schedule._amountOp); shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount re-codes the approx tolerance instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: scheduleModel.toExternal (api-models.ts) restates getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range dispatch as a reshaped nested ternary with a different endpoint choice; the isapprox branch in getScheduledAmount inlines getApproxNumberThreshold's formula.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts swapped roundSumBeforeDividing for an amountOp parameter and gained an isapprox branch; scheduleModel.toExternal in api-models.ts bypasses it with its own (now stale) rule.
